subject: research/chip-cutheadroom
professional: a senior logic-synthesis researcher (the kind who reviews for DAC/ICCAD/TCAD and knows ABC's rewrite and mockturtle's cut_rewriting). They would check first that the cut, MFFC and exact-cost definitions are the standard ones and implemented right, that the analysis can actually detect headroom when it exists (so a null is meaningful), that the parsed netlists are the circuits claimed, and whether the result is new against exact-synthesis cut rewriting already published

evidence.correctness: Every published number recomputes with code the author did not write. (1) Own NPN canonicalisation (own substitution code, not exact.py) gives 222 classes equal to the keys of exact_costs.json, and the induced cost distribution over all 65,536 functions is 10/60/456/2474/10624/24184/25008/2720 for costs 0..7, exactly Knuth TAOCP 4A sec. 7.1.2; brute-force circuit enumeration (no SAT) reproduces the exact cost of all 6,812 normal functions of cost <= 4 with 0 disagreements. (2) Own analyser (own Yosys JSON parse, inverters as free edge polarities, cut enumeration by leaf expansion, ABC-style reference-count MFFC) on Yosys 0.33 netlists: gates, w/room, cone>=3 and removable agree with results.json in 30 of 30 design/flow runs; the two headroom cones (mul6 resyn2 cut of 3 leaves, MFFC 4, f=0xe6e6 cost 3; lt16 resyn2 MFFC 3, f=0xf6f6 cost 2) have costs confirmed by the brute force. (3) Every one of the 30 netlists simulates correctly on 300 random vectors against Python reference semantics (+, *, <, popcount, <<, lowest-set-index priority). (4) Detection power: injecting k redundant XOR expansions into add16/mul6/pop8 default netlists yields removable exactly 2k for k = 1, 3, 5; and on 60 isolated random 4-input functions analyse() reports removable equal to gates - exact cost in 60/60 (mean gap 1.32, consistent with chip-exact4's 1.19). Not 4: no comparison against an established tool (ABC rewrite gain, mockturtle cut_rewriting) on the same netlists.
evidence.completeness: Claimed and checked: run.py reruns in 4.8 s (README says about 1 minute) and results.txt is byte-identical; figure.py regenerates headroom.svg byte-identical; 7 tests as stated (5 synthetic + 2 Yosys) all pass with Yosys 0.33 installed; exact_costs.json and exact.py are byte-identical to chip-exact4 as stated; headline sums (2,483 gates over 30 runs; cone>=3 range 4 to 52) recomputed from results.json. Live page https://marisstella.app/research/chip-cutheadroom/ could not be loaded (proxy 403), so not verified. No stubs or TODOs; Next steps are honestly listed as not done.
evidence.verification: `cd research/chip-cutheadroom && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`: without Yosys 'Ran 7 tests OK (skipped=2)'; with Yosys 0.33 'Ran 7 tests in 2.987s OK'. Six seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: 2 caught (dropping the disjointness check; dropping the primary-output exclusion from the MFFC), 4 survived: the MFFC rule itself (fanout[m] <= s -> fanout[m] & s, netlist.py:186), which moves summed removable over the 30 runs from 2 to 104 with every test green; the cut-size bound (<= k -> < k, :141); the cone>=3 threshold behind headline 3 (:206); and $_ORNOT_ semantics (:23). ANDNOT semantics are caught. No test pins results.json, and the Yosys tests skip silently where Yosys is absent (CI without it runs 5).
evidence.craft: Read netlist.py (208 lines), exact.py, designs.py, tests, run.py, figure.py. Small, stdlib-only, readable; flows and designs are data; cut enumeration and MFFC are the textbook ones. Defects: run.py:1 docstring says three ABC flows (there are five); figure.py:28 legend labels the 'fast' bars 'fast (strash; map)' though fast is abc -fast (numbers happen to match); exact.py imports pysat lazily without declaring it (unused at runtime here, fine but undocumented); in analyse the per-cut tuple carries a sorted-leaves element that is never used for tie-breaking; MFFC is a quadratic fixpoint rather than reference counting (fine at this size).
evidence.claims: Checked against files: headline 1 (0 in 28 runs, 1 in mul6/lt16 resyn2, 0.6%/1.2%, 2,483 gates) in results.txt and recomputed; headline 2 (82 vs 110 add16, 41 vs 71 prio16, -25%/-42%, headroom 0) in results.txt; table rows match; 'Yosys 0.33' matches; copies from chip-exact4 byte-identical; limitations (existence only, no reconstruction, six stylised blocks, gate count not area, 4-cuts only) are candid. Weaker: headline 3 'proposer would be wasted on these netlists ... every one is already exactly minimal' goes past the measurement, which is single-pass positive-gain only: it does not consider zero-gain replacements (ABC's rewrite -z exists because they unlock later gains) and 'exactly minimal' is really 'no cut's MFFC exceeds the exact cost'. The figure legend mislabels the fast flow. Prior work cited 'not re-read'.
evidence.fitness: Job: a researcher deciding whether an LLM/proposer loop should spend effort on exact small-cone rewrites of Yosys/ABC output. The code is clean, runs in 5 s, and the null result survives my independent re-implementation and a detection-power test, so it is something one can build on. But nearest prior work is not engaged: Riener, Haaswijk, Mishchenko, De Micheli and Soeken, 'On-the-fly and DAG-aware: rewriting Boolean networks with exact synthesis' (DATE 2019, mockturtle cut_rewriting), and Haaswijk et al. 'SAT-based exact synthesis' (TCAD 2020) already do 4-cut (and larger) exact-synthesis rewriting after ABC on EPFL benchmarks and report residual gains; Cong and Minkovich (FPGA 2007 / TCAD) study optimality gaps of synthesis with constructed-optimum circuits. Against that literature a null on six stylised 6-to-16-bit blocks, after a cut-based mapper that already selects per-cut matches, is expected rather than new; no standard benchmark (EPFL, ISCAS) is run. Preliminary and below the PhD bar, as the README itself says.
evidence.domain: The method matches standard logic-synthesis practice: k-feasible cuts, MFFC with PO references, NPN-class exact costs over the full 2-input basis with free inverters (consistent with the 8-type gate library, which covers all 10 non-degenerate 2-input functions up to operand order), and a disjoint greedy for a one-pass bound. Departures a practitioner would flag: no zero-gain or iterated moves, so 'no headroom' is a single-pass local optimum not a fixed point of rewriting; gate count with free inverters rather than mapped area; no standard benchmark suite. These are mostly disclosed.

verdict: A small, correct, reproducible null result. Every number recomputes with code the author did not write: the exact-cost table matches Knuth's distribution for all 65,536 functions and a brute-force enumeration for every cost <= 4; an independent analyser agrees with results.json on all 30 netlists; all 30 netlists simulate correctly; and the analysis provably detects injected redundancy (2k for k injections) and reproduces chip-exact4's isolated-function gap. run.py and figure.py reproduce byte-identically in 5 s. It misses the bar on verification: 4 of 6 seeded mutants survive, including the MFFC rule itself, whose corruption inflates the headline from 2 to 104 removable gates with all tests green. As research it is preliminary: six stylised blocks, no standard benchmarks, no engagement with published exact-synthesis cut rewriting, and headline 3 slightly overreaches a single-pass positive-gain measurement.
